label: <DEL> step when the first original token is c/q/f/n/w/l/s
explanation: Almost entirely a delimiter-step unit: 93% of activation mass is on the <DEL> input (step L, where the model must output original token 0). Whether it fires there is set by which token is about to be output (the first original token). Rates are highest for c (about 10%), then q, n, f, then w, l, s; it is near zero for most other first tokens, including digits. The top activations all start with c (often with h at position 2). Only about 11% of <DEL> steps are active overall, and even for the favored first tokens the precision is about 43%, so other context (it fires less often with longer L and with more digits) also gates it, and I could not capture that cleanly. A small remainder (about 7% of mass) comes from original-phase steps at t=3..6 on inputs g, p, i, j. It essentially never fires during the copy phase (after the delimiter) or at t<3.
